title: Signed within-visit pulse-pressure drift does not improve cross-cycle DSST prediction in NHANES
abstract: In 1265 NHANES 2011–2012 adults aged 60+ and 1373 separately sampled 2013–2014 adults, signed first-to-third pulse-pressure change did not improve frozen-model DSST prediction beyond demographics, body size, average blood pressure, pressure variability, MAP drift and pulse. Target weighted MSE increased from 161.670 to 161.918 (+0.153%); source-and-target PSU-refit bootstrap limits for the MSE difference were [-0.564, 3.705]. This is a negative test of one linear feature in reused cross-sectional cohorts, not evidence that cuff dynamics contain no cognitive information.
